translation_notes: prefixes: TOOLKIT_NS->toolkit, OWL->owl, PROV->prov, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, XSD->xsd
g.subjects(RDF.type, RDF.Statement) -> m{ ?stmt rdf:type rdf:Statement }(g), one-step traversal projecting the subject.

the three '(x, p, o) not in g' existence guards -> bool(m{ {x} p {o} }(g)) each, per the trav_existence idiom, kept as three separate islands rather than folded into one multi-pattern m{ } (folding into a join would change which check short-circuits first and would require re-deriving the AND from a single solution set -- not the same program).
g.triples((stmt, PROV.wasDerivedFrom, None)) and g.triples((deriv, TOOLKIT_NS.premise, None)) -> m{ {x} p ?y }(g), the trav_one_step idiom the stratum targets.
every next(g.objects(...), None) -> m{ {x} p ?o }(g).first(): .first() already returns None on an empty solution set, matching next(..., None) exactly.
needed a context shim (helpers.py) for _parse_term, defined a few lines below the extracted region in the source file but not part of it.

fixture.ttl covers two derivations for one reified statement (one premise complete, one missing rdf:object and so excluded), a neighbouring reified statement for a different triple, and a reified statement with no prov:wasDerivedFrom at all (inner zero-solution case); driver.py adds a third call whose (s, p, o) matches no statement at all (outer zero-solution case). explain_triple's first argument is a file path rather than a graph, so the calls are written by hand instead of using the generic fixture= wiring.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `Graph().parse(...)` chained; the three `continue` guards merged into one `if ... or ... or ...: continue`; `next(g.objects(x, P), None)` -> `g.value(x, P)` (six reads); `g.triples((x, P, None))` with `_, _, y` unpacking -> `g.objects(x, P)`; the premises loop becomes a comprehension of `[g.value(prem, term) for term in (RDF.subject, RDF.predicate, RDF.object)]`, filtered with `all(premise)` (same truth test as `ps and pp and po`) and stringified with `list(map(str, premise))` in the dict. s, p, o are still computed once before the loop, so _parse_term raises (or not) exactly as before.

optimized.ldpy: the rdf:type loop and the three existence guards become ONE multi-pattern island `m{ ?stmt a rdf:Statement ; rdf:subject f<{subject}> ; rdf:predicate f<{predicate}> ; rdf:object {_parse_term(obj)} }` (nested-loop join in written order, so statements come in the same order; the three bound patterns match at most once each). Its interpolations are evaluated once when the island is built, so the s/p/o locals go too. This is the exception to the symmetry rule: only the island joins the type scan and the guards in one read, and only its evaluate-once interpolation lets s/p/o be inlined without re-evaluating _parse_term per statement.

optimized.ldpy: the two one-step loops are `m{ {stmt} prov:wasDerivedFrom ?deriv }` and `m{ {deriv} toolkit:premise ?prem }` with `@graph g`; the single-value reads stay `g.value(deriv, toolkit:rule)` etc. with prefixed names, and the premise terms tuple is `(rdf:subject, rdf:predicate, rdf:object)` (rule 4: `m{ ... }.first()` measured longer than `g.value(x, prefix:name)`; `g.objects(x, prefix:name)` measured longer than the m{ } loops).
The premises are not folded into a join with the derivation: a premise with two rdf:subject values would then yield two rows where g.value takes one.
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py drops Iterable, Optional, Sequence, Tuple (typing), BNode, Literal, Variable (rdflib) and OWL, RDFS, XSD (rdflib.namespace); keeps Namespace for TOOLKIT_NS.

optimized_header.ldpy drops the same typing names, every rdflib name but Graph (URIRef replaced by f<…>, Namespace unused since TOOLKIT_NS is the toolkit: prefix), the whole rdflib.namespace import, and the unused @prefix owl:, rdfs:, xsd:; keeps @prefix toolkit:, prov:, rdf:.
